name: Yutanduchi de Guerrero Mixtec
confidence_why: Nothing describes stress in Yutanduchi Mixtec itself: the only statement that covers it is Josserand's 1983 family-wide claim that the Mixtec couplet carries stress on its first syllable, known here only as quoted by Carroll (2015) and Penner (2019), while McKendry (2001), the one first-hand Yutanduchi source, is does not discuss stress.

catalog_quote: Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as “composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two,” implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior. Besides the data from Santo Domingo Nuxaa shown in (4.2), several other descriptions support the characterization of stress in Mixtec as falling on the first vowel of the couplet. ... In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec. [Carroll 2015:86] ... Furthermore, one Mixtec variety, that of Yoloxochitl (Yol) has been described to have final stress, partially on the basis of these same distributional properties (DiCanio p.c., DiCanio et al. submitted). [Carroll 2015:87] [Table A.2, p. 276, Community / Abbreviation / Josserand / ISO code / Group] Yutanduchi de Guerrero Ytd Yutn mab Alta:E [Penner 2019:91-92] Stress on the penultimate syllable or vowel of the couplet (or similar structure with a different descriptive label) is reported in the vast majority of Mixtec descriptions (e.g. Jicaltepec Mixtec, Bradley 1977:17; ... Nuyoo Mixtec, Harris & Harris 2006:2), and Josserand 1983:180 posits stress on the penult syllable of the couplet for Proto-Mixtec.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: lines 5443-5446 (printed p. 86, sec. 4.2.1) read exactly 'Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as "composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two," implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior.'; line 5490 (still p. 86) has 'In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec.'; line 16819 (Table A.2, printed p. 276) has the row 'Yutanduchi de Guerrero Ytd Yutn mab Alta:E' (the only other Ytd hit, line 17028, is a map label). All three pieces of the reported quote are verbatim at the stated locators (the '[..]' elision spans the intervening survey of Ayutl…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the first syllable of the bimoraic/disyllabic root 'couplet', i.e. the penultimate syllable of canonical disyllabic roots; this is Josserand's family-wide generalization over her 120-town dialect survey, which includes Yutanduchi de Guerrero (code Yutn, Eastern Alta). No Yutanduchi-specific stress description exists.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Yutanduchi; Carroll notes for other varieties that vocalic enclitics may or may not shift stress (Silacayoapan, Alacatlatzala) and that Atatlahuca polysyllables take penultimate stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the root couplet (stem), not the phonological word with clitics; statement is comparative/family-level, not based on Yutanduchi citation forms.
new_statements.identity_note: All evidence refers to the town variety of Yutanduchi de Guerrero (Josserand code Yutn; MixteCoDB yuta11; INALI 'tu'un savi de Yutanduchi de Guerrero'), which is exactly Glottolog yuta1240 / ISO mab (Eastern Alta Mixtec). The stress statement itself is Josserand's pan-Mixtec generalization, not a description of this variety.
